title: Measles Outbreak Spreads as US Loses Disease-Free Status
subtitle: Families and health experts struggle to respond as cases rise across the country

summary.en: The United States has officially lost its measles-free status after 26 years due to a major national outbreak. Virginia recently reported its first measles-associated death of 2026, adding to a growing number of fatalities. Health experts warn that declining vaccination rates are the primary cause of this public health crisis. Many parents are now changing their daily routines to protect children who are too young to be vaccinated. Officials emphasize that high vaccination levels are necessary to keep the community safe from the virus.
summary.zh: 美國在維持二十六年無麻疹狀態後，因全國性的大規模爆發而正式喪失此地位。維吉尼亞州近期通報了二零二六年首起與麻疹相關的死亡案例，死亡人數持續攀升。衛生專家警告，疫苗接種率下降是這場公共衛生危機的主因。許多家長現正改變日常生活習慣，以保護年紀太小而無法接種疫苗的兒童。官員強調，維持高疫苗接種率對於保護社區免受病毒侵害至關重要。

paragraphs.en: The United States is facing a serious public health challenge as measles continues to spread across the country. On Friday, health officials in Virginia reported the state’s first measles-associated death of 2026. According to The Guardian Health, the child was four years old or younger. While the state health department did not share specific details about the child’s vaccination history to protect the family’s privacy, the event highlights the growing danger of this infectious disease.
paragraphs.zh: 美國正面臨嚴峻的公共衛生挑戰，麻疹疫情持續在全國蔓延。週五，維吉尼亞州的衛生官員通報了該州二零二六年首起與麻疹相關的死亡案例。根據衛報健康版（The Guardian Health）報導，該名兒童年僅四歲或更小。儘管州衛生部門為了保護家屬隱私，未透露該名兒童的疫苗接種細節，但此事件凸顯了這種傳染病日益嚴重的威脅。

paragraphs.en: This recent death is part of a much larger national problem. Earlier this week, health officials confirmed that the United States has lost its measles-free status after 26 years. This status was removed because the number of cases has reached a level that is no longer considered under control. According to NPR Health, more than 5,000 cases have been reported across the country so far this year. Pennsylvania remains the hardest-hit state, reporting 1,631 cases and eight deaths. Other states, including Wisconsin and New York, have also reported deaths related to the virus.
paragraphs.zh: 這起近期的死亡案例只是全國性大問題的一環。本週稍早，衛生官員證實美國在維持二十六年無麻疹狀態後，已正式喪失此地位。這項地位被撤銷是因為病例數已達到無法控制的程度。根據美國國家公共廣播電台健康版（NPR Health）報導，今年全國迄今已通報超過五千起病例。賓夕法尼亞州仍是受創最嚴重的地區，共計通報一千六百三十一起病例及八起死亡案例。包括威斯康辛州與紐約州在內的其他州，也通報了與該病毒相關的死亡事件。

paragraphs.en: There is currently some confusion regarding the total number of deaths nationwide. The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has confirmed six measles-associated deaths, but this number does not match the higher figures reported by individual states. The Guardian Health noted that this difference exists because the CDC, under the leadership of health secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., has started using different data sources to track mortality. This change in how information is collected makes it difficult for the public to understand the full scale of the crisis.
paragraphs.zh: 目前對於全國死亡總數存在一些混亂。美國疾病管制與預防中心（CDC）已證實六起與麻疹相關的死亡案例，但此數字與各州自行通報的較高數據並不吻合。衛報健康版指出，這種差異存在的原因是，在衛生部長小羅伯特·甘迺迪（Robert F. Kennedy Jr.）的領導下，疾病管制與預防中心已開始採用不同的數據來源來追蹤死亡率。這種資訊收集方式的改變，使得大眾難以理解這場危機的全貌。

paragraphs.en: For many parents, the outbreak is changing how they live their daily lives. Because children must be at least one year old to receive the measles vaccine, many infants remain unprotected. NPR Health interviewed parents who are now avoiding public places like libraries, stores, and airports to keep their young children safe. Some families have even cancelled travel plans to avoid crowded areas where the virus might spread. Dr. Joanna Parga-Belinkie, a neonatologist in Philadelphia, explained that the situation feels similar to the restrictions people faced during the COVID-19 pandemic.
paragraphs.zh: 對許多家長而言，這場疫情正在改變他們的日常生活。由於兒童必須年滿一歲才能接種麻疹疫苗，許多嬰幼兒仍處於無保護狀態。美國國家公共廣播電台健康版採訪了一些家長，他們為了保護年幼子女的安全，現在正避免前往圖書館、商店與機場等公共場所。有些家庭甚至取消了旅遊計畫，以避開病毒可能傳播的擁擠區域。費城的新生兒科醫師喬安娜·帕加-貝林基（Joanna Parga-Belinkie）解釋說，這種情況讓人感覺就像新冠肺炎（COVID-19）疫情期間所面臨的限制一樣。

paragraphs.en: Experts point to one main reason for this situation: a drop in vaccination rates. Dr. Parga-Belinkie told NPR Health that a community needs 95% of its members to be vaccinated to effectively stop the spread of measles. When fewer people get the vaccine, the virus finds it easier to move from person to person. Data from Virginia supports this view, showing that of the 220 cases reported in the state, 179 involved people who were not vaccinated. Frederic Bertley, an immunologist and chief executive of the Center of Science and Industry, told The Guardian Health that the virus is gaining a strong foothold and becoming a serious, growing problem for the entire nation.
paragraphs.zh: 專家指出造成此局面的主要原因：疫苗接種率下降。帕加-貝林基醫師告訴美國國家公共廣播電台健康版，一個社區需要百分之九十五的成員接種疫苗，才能有效阻斷麻疹傳播。當接種疫苗的人數減少，病毒就更容易在人與人之間擴散。維吉尼亞州的數據支持了這一觀點，該州通報的二百二十起病例中，有一百七十九起涉及未接種疫苗者。免疫學家兼科學與工業中心執行長弗雷德里克·伯特利（Frederic Bertley）向衛報健康版表示，該病毒正取得強大立足點，並成為全國日益嚴重的重大問題。

paragraphs.en: In Virginia, the outbreak is not spread evenly. Health officials report that the central region of the state is seeing the most activity. Buckingham County has recorded 127 cases, while the neighboring Charlotte County has reported 34. These localized outbreaks show how quickly the disease can move through a community when vaccination levels are low.
paragraphs.zh: 在維吉尼亞州，疫情並非均勻分佈。衛生官員指出，該州中部地區疫情最為嚴重。白金漢郡已記錄到一百二十七起病例，而鄰近的夏洛特郡則通報了三十四起。這些局部爆發顯示，當疫苗接種率偏低時，疾病在社區中擴散的速度有多快。

paragraphs.en: As the country moves forward, health officials are urging parents to follow recommended vaccination schedules. The vaccine is highly effective, with a 97% success rate in preventing the disease after two doses. However, until more of the population is protected, the risk of infection remains high. For now, parents are left to make difficult decisions about how to balance their daily activities with the need to keep their children safe from a disease that most people thought was a thing of the past. The situation serves as a stark reminder of the importance of public health measures in maintaining a safe society.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著國家持續應對疫情，衛生官員敦促家長遵循建議的疫苗接種時程。該疫苗效果極佳，接種兩劑後預防疾病的成功率高達百分之九十七。然而，在更多人口獲得保護之前，感染風險依然很高。目前，家長們被迫做出艱難決定，如何在日常生活與保護子女免受這種大多數人以為已成過去的疾病威脅之間取得平衡。此情況嚴正提醒了公共衛生措施對於維護社會安全的重要性。

keyTerms.definitionEn: Most severely affected by a negative event or situation.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 受創最嚴重的；受影響最大的。
keyTerms.noteZh: 此處為複合形容詞，描述受疫情影響最深的地區。文中：Pennsylvania remains the hardest-hit state, reporting 1,631 cases and eight deaths.

keyTerms.definitionEn: A strong position that makes it possible to advance or establish something further.
keyTerms.noteZh: 原意為攀岩時腳踩的地方，此處比喻病毒在社區中站穩腳跟並持續擴散。文中：Frederic Bertley, an immunologist and chief executive of the Center of Science and Industry, told The Guardian Health that the virus is gaining a strong foothold and becoming a serious, growing problem for the entire nation.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Something that no longer exists or happens.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 已成往事；不再存在的事物。
keyTerms.noteZh: 用來形容人們以為已經消失、不再發生的疾病。文中：For now, parents are left to make difficult decisions about how to balance their daily activities with the need to keep their children safe from a disease that most people thought was a thing of the past.

quiz.question: According to the article, why is there a discrepancy between the CDC's national measles death count and the figures reported by individual states?

options.A: Individual states are intentionally inflating their death counts to receive more funding.
options.B: The CDC is currently using different data collection methods than those used by individual states.
options.C: The CDC only counts deaths of children under the age of four, while states count all ages.
options.D: The CDC has stopped updating its database due to the high volume of cases across the country.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第三段，CDC 的死亡統計數字與各州不符，是因為在 Robert F. Kennedy Jr. 的領導下，CDC 開始採用不同的數據來源來追蹤死亡率。選項 A 文中未提及；選項 C 錯誤，文中僅提到維吉尼亞州的死亡案例是四歲以下，並未說明 CDC 的統計標準；選項 D 錯誤，CDC 並未停止更新，只是數據來源改變了。

quiz.question: Based on the information provided, what can be inferred about the current state of measles vaccination in the United States?

options.A: The vaccine is no longer effective at preventing the measles virus.
options.B: Most Americans are choosing not to vaccinate their children due to personal beliefs.
options.C: The overall vaccination rate in the country has likely fallen below the 95% threshold required for community immunity.
options.D: The government has made vaccination mandatory for all citizens to regain their measles-free status.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章第五段指出，免疫學家 Frederic Bertley 提到病毒正取得立足點，且 Dr. Parga-Belinkie 指出社區需要 95% 的接種率才能有效阻斷傳播。由於目前疫情嚴重且全國已失去無麻疹狀態，可推論全國接種率已不足以達到群體免疫。選項 A 與文章第七段提到的 97% 成功率矛盾；選項 B 無法從文中證實；選項 D 文中並未提到強制接種政策。

quiz.question: In the fifth paragraph, what does the phrase 'gaining a strong foothold' mean?

options.A: Becoming firmly established and difficult to remove.
options.B: Moving rapidly from one location to another.
options.C: Losing its ability to infect new people.
options.D: Developing a new method of transmission.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。在第五段中，作者使用 'gaining a strong foothold' 來形容病毒在社區中的擴散情況。'Foothold' 原意為立足點，在此比喻病毒已經在人群中紮根且難以根除。選項 B 雖然病毒在傳播，但該片語強調的是「穩固」而非「移動」；選項 C 與句意相反；選項 D 文中並未提及病毒演化出新傳播方式。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of this article?

options.A: The U.S. government is failing to provide adequate medical supplies to hospitals.
options.B: Measles is a historical disease that has been successfully eradicated in the United States.
options.C: A decline in vaccination rates has led to a serious measles outbreak that is disrupting daily life and public health.
options.D: The CDC is currently undergoing a leadership change that has improved public health data accuracy.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。本文的核心在於報導美國麻疹疫情的復燃，並強調這主要是由疫苗接種率下降所導致，且這種情況嚴重影響了民眾的日常生活與公共衛生安全。選項 A 非文章重點；選項 B 與事實相反，因為美國已失去無麻疹狀態；選項 D 僅是文中提到的一個細節，並非文章的主旨。
